Forty-six. You came back where you were, so I stay where I was. That's my last number. Take it, or I pack up and we're done.

Ay, hijo, ya casi nos damos la mano. Mira, 25 P y no se hable más, que me caes bien y tu abuela me ha ganado el corazón. Tráeme tus repetidas la semana que viene, cariño. Y come algo antes de las nueve y media, ¿eh?

Ay, hijo, fifteen again, with that same pretty smile. Mira, 23 P and I wrap it in paper. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, you look like a little bird.

Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo, pero con gracia. Sixteen, no. Mira — 22 P, and I wrap it pretty with the paper I save for my favourites. Forty years I sit here, I know a good home when I see one. Now, cariño... have you eaten something today?

Ay, diecisiete, cariño, you climb like a little snail. Mira — 21 P, and I wrap it with my good paper. Forty years here, hijo, and still I give too much away. El Chato laughs at me. Now promise me, you eat something today. You look like a little bird.
Noventa y dos. Un paso tuyo, un paso mío. Siempre igual, ¿eh? La carta sigue limpia. Tú decides.
You move, I move. 91 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.

Ay, cariño, eighteen again? You are stubborn like my Pepe, que en paz descanse. I stay at twenty-three P — and I wrap it nice, with a little bag. A whole page, almost complete, hijo. Take it, and go eat something warm, sí?

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my grandson! Look — 26 P, and I throw in a smile for free. Remember, swap your duplicates; a full page is worth much more than loose cards. And pass by El Chato tonight at half past nine, he likes honest traders like you.
Look, 25 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay cariño, you are a sweet one, but 25 P is my number today — the same for my own nietos. Eat something, you look thin! And remember, swap those duplicates; a full page is worth much more. Pass by El Chato tonight at half past nine, he likes honest traders.

Ay, hijo, you push so gently I cannot be cross. Look — 24 P, and that is me being a grandmother, not a seller. Go eat something afterwards, sí? And swap those duplicates; a full page is worth much more. El Chato opens at half past nine tonight.
Ninety-six. That's me moving. Your turn, and make it worth watching.
Noventa y dos. You moved, I moved. Card's still clean. Your turn.
Noventa. Last one. You walk, I walk, card stays with me. Decide.

Ay, hijo, qué labia tienes. Twenty-five, 25 P, and I wrap it nice for you. Look — the corners are perfect, nobody kept them like this. My Chato next door sells packs if you want more, but this page is special. ¿Seguro que has comido?
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres... pero mira, 24 P ya es cariño puro. Es mi último, de verdad. Esta página te va a dar muchas tardes bonitas, ya verás. Y si tienes repetidas, tráemelas el domingo, que algo te busco. ¿Trato hecho, hijo?
You moved three. I move one. Ninety-six. That's how it works here.

¡Ay, cariño, qué bueno que desayunaste! Nineteen is too much for my little table, hijo. Let me say 6 for El Portero — un poquito more, because you are kind. And advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, sí?
¡Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres! But eighteen, no, no — my pocket is small and my table is old. Six, cariño, six is what I can give for El Portero. Take it, and come back next Sunday for a coffee, sí?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P.

¡Churros, qué rico, hijo! But six is my last word, cariño — six for El Portero, and no more. If you say no, we part friends and no hard feelings, sí? El Chato opens at half past nine tonight; he likes straight traders. ¿Qué dices, six?

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Guantería Antigua, one of my favourites, I have kept her nice and clean. For you, twenty-nine P. My grandson started his album with this very card, ¿sabes?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P.

Ay, hecho, hijo! Twenty-five P, and she is yours. Take good care of her. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates with the other niños. Now go, eat something. Come back Sunday!
You again. La Tabacalera. Thirty-three. That's the number, not an opening for poetry.
You moved three. I moved nothing. Thirty-three. Packs are walking off this table today, amigo.
You move, I move. 32 P.
You moved one. So did I. Thirty-two. Card's still here, but not for long.
You move, I move. 31 P.
Thirty-one. Done. La Tabacalera's yours — you dealt straight, I remember that.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Sit a moment. For you I have the Escaparate de Serrano — a beauty — twelve P. And one little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Ay, cariño, you bargain like my own nieto! Look — nine P, and I wrap it nice for you. Have you eaten today? Take it home, finish that page, and come tell me Sunday. A full page, hijo, that is where the treasure is.
Oh, oh... 9 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look at this one — La Vía Láctea, the shiny stars one. The children always want her. For you, 29 P. My Sunday price, hijo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P.

Ay, hijo, you are going backwards! First thirteen, now twelve — soon you will ask me to pay you, ¿eh? Mira, La Vía Láctea stays at 26 P. She shines, cariño. Sit, rest a little. Have you eaten something today?

Ay, hola cariño, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one is my Neighbourhood pack — good cards to begin, thirty P. My grandson started with this same pack, and now he beats me every Sunday. Take your time, no hurry here.
Guantería Antigua. Thirty-three. You want it or you want to look?
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
One peseta. That's your move? Mine stays. Thirty-three.
One step from me too. Thirty-one. Keep crawling, we'll be here till the market closes.
You move, I move. 30 P.
Twenty-nine. Guantería Antigua, that's the last word I have. You say no, I pack up and we're done.
You again. Guantería Antigua. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price.
¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, Perrito con Abrigo, my favourite little dog in his coat. Twelve P and he is yours. No hurry, hijo, look at all of them first.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, Mercado de San Ildefonso. A pretty card, hijo, good to start an album. Twenty-nine P for you. My hands have passed this table forty years, so take your time looking.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 25 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, twelve! My old heart. No, no — twenty-five P, that is my little price, and I say it with a smile. Take it, put it in your album, and swap your duplicates with the other niños. A full page, cariño, that is the treasure.

Buenos días. Fifty-one. Claro.

Thirteen. That is what it is worth. I have the Tienda de Discos if you prefer trading to dreaming.
You came down two. That is not meeting, that is leaning. Thirteen, same as before. Tienda de Discos, thirteen. Take it or walk, amigo.
Three, this time. Still leaning. My number has not moved either. Tienda de Discos, thirteen. Straight deal, today, no theatre.
Three again. You call that bigger? I move when you move, and you have not. Thirteen. Tienda de Discos. Still today, if you want it.

Three from you. One from me. That is the arithmetic, amigo.

Fourteen. Tienda de Discos. Today.
Fifteen. Tienda de Discos. That is my last word, amigo — no more arithmetic. Say no and I pack up and we are finished today.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, have you eaten? Look here — this one, the Huevos Rotos, very pretty card, twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, qué zalamero eres, hijo. Mira, ten P and we are friends — the Huevos Rotos goes home with you. Forty years I sit here, and still the pretty cards make me soft. Ten P, cariño. And eat something before the market closes, ¿eh?
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten? No? Later, later. Look at this one, Huevos Rotos — a beautiful card, very popular with the little ones. Twelve P, hijo. My grandson started his album with this very same card.

Ay, qué bien, diez P entonces, hijo. Take it, take it — es tuyo. My grandson started just like this, one little card, and now his album is full. Come back next Sunday and show me yours, eh? And eat something, cariño, you look hungry.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, Café en Goya, very pretty card, my favourite of the set. For you, twelve P. My Sundays here are forty years now, and I still love giving the good ones to beginners.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.
You're Carmen's friend. Fiesta de San Cayetano, 97 P.
Your friends don't pay my rent. You moved fourteen, I move one. 96 P.
Six from you. One from me. 95 P. That's how it works, amigo.
Nice numbers. Not mine. You moved six, I move three. 92 P. Cash is cash, amigo — but it buys at my price.
Two from you, two from me. 90 P. Market says what you want it to say. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Shop around if you like.
Two from you, two from me. 88 P. No back and forth — your words, amigo. Cash out, card's yours.
Two from you, two from me. 86 P. Same dance, amigo. Cash out, card's yours.
Two from you, two from me. 84 P. You keep saying "no back and forth," amigo. Put the cash out and prove it.
82. Done. Fiesta de San Cayetano is yours, amigo. You deal straight — I remember that.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this Neighbourhood pack, thirty P — good cards for starting, I promise. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates with the other niños. Take your time looking.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, have you eaten? Look at this one, Tienda de Discos, very pretty, very hard to find. For you, 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Oh, oh... 26 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, hijo, you go down, not up! No, no, 26 P, same as before — I cannot go chasing you downhill, cariño. Think of it: with this card your page is finished, and a finished page is worth so much more. Now, have you eaten something today?
Cine Doré. Ninety-seven. You've seen worse cards cost more.
You move, I move. 97 P.
One peseta? That is not moving, that is twitching. Ninety-six. Match me properly or we both go home.
Another peseta. You are counting in crumbs. Ninety-four. I move when you move, and you barely move.
You move, I move. 93 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one is special — Guantería Antigua, a beautiful old card, I keep it under the cloth. For you, twenty-nine P. My grandson loved this one when he was small.

Ay, hijo, twelve... that is too little for this one, you know? But I don't like to argue, I never did. Look — twenty-seven P, and I wrap it nice in paper for you. My grandson kept his in a shoebox, poor thing. ¿Sí, cariño?

Ay, qué cariñoso eres, hijo. Trece... no, no llega. Mira, twenty-six P, and I put it in paper so it travels safe. This card waited many Sundays under my cloth for someone like you. ¿Sí, cariño? Later you tell me if you ate.

Ay, cariño, catorce... todavía no. Mira, twenty-five P, and I wrap it in paper myself. This little card has seen forty years of Sundays on this table, it deserves a good home. ¿Sí, hijo? And later you tell me if you have eaten something.

Gracias, cariño, qué cosas más bonitas dices. Pero quince... no llega, hijo. Mira, veinticinco P, como antes, y te la envuelvo en papel con mis manos. Esta cartita merece estar contigo. ¿Sí, cariño? Y dime luego si has comido algo.

Ay, hijo, dieciséis... no puede ser. Mira, veinticuatro P, y te la envuelvo yo misma en papel. Pero esta es mi última, cariño, de verdad. Si no, la guardo otra vez bajo el paño y no pasa nada. ¿Sí? Y dime luego si has comido.
You again. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. Ninety-seven. Good card, straight price. Take it or walk.
Ninety-seven. Yo no me he movido. Tú sí. La Heroína vale lo que vale. Sesenta y tres no la compra.
Cuatro subes tú. Yo bajo uno... por ahora. Noventa y seis. Mueve más, muevo más. Así funciona.

Buenos días, hijo! Qué amable, bringing me something. Have you eaten? Sit a moment. For La Galería I can give you 12 P, cariño. It is a pretty card, I like it very much. Tell me, how long have you been collecting?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 13 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Look, 14 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Look, 14 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten today? Look here, this one, the Taxi Blanco. A good card to start with, very pretty. Twelve P for you. My grandson started with this very same one, pobrecito, he never swapped it.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 11 P.

Ay, está bien, hijo — ten P, we have a deal! Take the Taxi Blanco, she is yours. Keep her in a sleeve, eh? And come back Sunday, I always have something for beginners. Now go eat something, cariño, you look too thin.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, very pretty card, my favourite corner of Madrid. For you, five P. A good start for your album, hijo.

Ay, hijo, you are too generous! Eleven? No, no. Five P is what I said, and five P it is. I do not take more from a young collector starting an album. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, cariño. Come back next Sunday, eh?

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing money at me! No. Plaza del Dos de Mayo is five P, the same as before. Put those extra coins away, buy churros. Take the card, enjoy it, and come tell me how your album grows, hijo.

Ay, cariño, my true price is the only price: five P. No secrets at this table! Take the card, bring the churros Sunday, we talk about your abuelo. And listen — El Chato next door opens for everybody at half past nine tonight. He likes straight traders, hijo.

Ay, hijo, what a stubborn one you are! Then we stay stuck, because my card is five P and not a céntimo more. Take it, put it in your album tonight. And eat something, cariño — you look thin. Sunday, churros, and you tell me everything.

Ay, cariño, no helpers here, only me. Five P — that is my last word, and if you say no, I put the card back in the box, con cariño. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, hijo!

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? No? Later, later. This one here, the Taxi Blanco — very pretty card, my favourite. For you, twelve P. My grandson he started with this one, now he beats everybody, hijo.
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Look, 10 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You again. La Chulapa. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
One peseta is not moving. Thirty-three. Still thirty-three.
No. 32 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirty-two. I already moved. Your steps are small, mine was bigger. Thirty-two, cash, and it's yours.
You move, I move. 31 P.
One peseta from you, one from me. Thirty. La Chulapa, thirty. Keep walking that way and we'll meet before dark.
You move, I move. 29 P.
Twenty-eight. Last one. You moved one, I moved one — that's the end of it. Take it, or I pack up and we're done.

¡Ay, hijo, qué majo! Sí, he comido, gracias. El sobre de barrio te lo dejo en 30 primas, cariño. Y toma, un regalito: "Plaza del Dos de Mayo", por ser tan amable conmigo. El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media esta noche.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me recuerdas a mi nieto. Mira, te lo dejo en 25 primas y tan amigos. Y un consejo: guarda tus repetidas y cámbialas, que una página completa vale mucho más que los cromos sueltos. ¿Seguro que has comido bien, hijo?

Ay, hijo, qué cabezota eres, igualito que mi nieto. Mira, 24 primas y no se hable más, cariño. Es un buen sobre, ya verás. Y esta noche pásate por El Chato, al lado; abre a las nueve y media y trata bien a quien cambia de frente. Come algo antes, ¿eh?

Ay, cariño, cómo me mareas, pero con esa sonrisa... 23 primas y cerramos, hijo. Llévatelo contento. Guarda las repetidas, que a alguien le faltan y valen oro. Y pásate esta noche por El Chato, que abre a las nueve y media. ¡Pero come algo antes, por Dios!

Ay, hijo, ya no puedo más, que me sacas los colores. 22 primas, y esta es mi última, de verdad. Si no, lo guardo y tan amigos, cariño, sin enfado. Piénsalo. Y esta noche, El Chato, a las nueve y media. ¡Pero cena algo antes, por Dios!
Noche de Movida. Ninety-seven. You looked at it twice already — I noticed.
Fair? You looked at it twice. Noche de Movida, ninety-seven. That is the number.
No. 95 P, and I'm being generous.
You moved. So did I. Ninety-three. Noche de Movida does not sit here long.
Done. 89 P.

¡Buenos días, hijo! Qué amable eres. Mira, for you, Té Moruno — five P, nothing more. And take this one too, El Organillero, a little regalo from me; he played music on my street when I was small. ¿Has comido ya, cariño? You look hungry.

¡Churros! Qué rico, hijo. Mira, I am old and simple with numbers — Té Moruno, five P, that is what I can say. The card will sit here with love, I promise. Children will come and look at it every Sunday. ¿Qué dices, cariño?

Ay, cariño, qué bueno eres bajando así. But I am the same old woman with the same old words: Té Moruno, five P. That is my offer, hijo, con todo mi corazón. Keep El Organillero either way — he is yours now.

Ay, hijo, qué paciencia tienes conmigo. Mira, I stretch a little for you, because you have a good heart — Té Moruno, six P. That is me being generous, cariño, con todo mi corazón. Then you go eat something proper, ¿sí? Not only churros.

¡Cocido, qué bien, hijo! Eso sí alimenta. Mira, cariño, I already stretched for you — Té Moruno, six P, that is my word and I keep it. No prisa, piénsalo tranquilo. I am here every Sunday, same table, same old woman.

Ay, cariño, qué álbum más bonito vas haciendo. Un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, hijo. But Té Moruno, six P. That is my last word; if no, we leave it, con cariño igual.
Abuela sent you. Bueno. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. Silver pack, clean. You want it or you want to look?
I'm not Abuela. And I'm selling, not buying. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. That's the number.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the table does not bite. Have you eaten today? Look here — my Neighbourhood pack, very nice cards for someone starting out. Thirty P, and I throw in a little story for free. What do you say, hijo?

Look, 26 P. My grandchildren would pay more! And take this, a little present from me: Huevos Rotos. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, you flatter an old woman! Eleven, no, no — these cards have travelled far. Twenty-five P, and that is me being soft because you have a nice face. Have you eaten? Go see El Chato tonight at half past nine, he likes honest traders like you.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 24 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, hijo, you have a good heart, and I like your friends already. Twenty-three P — and that is my last word, cariño. If no, we part as friends and I keep the pack. Go eat something. El Chato opens at half past nine; he likes straight traders.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten today? Look here, this one, Mercado de la Paz, very pretty card, my favourite. For you, twelve P. My daughter learned the game with that very card, hijo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 13 P.
You again. Las Vistillas, thirty-three. That's the number. Take it or walk.
You move, I move. 33 P.
Twenty-seven isn't moving. Thirty-three. Same number as before, same number next time. Las Vistillas doesn't get cheaper because you ask twice.
You again. Fiesta de San Cayetano. Ninety-seven. Good card, clean corners. Take it or look somewhere else.
You move, I move. 96 P.
You came up fourteen, I come down one. That's how it works. Ninety-five.
Ninety-one. You moved two, I moved two. Clean. Say yes and take the card.
Done. 91 P.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come! Have you eaten? Look, this one is La Vía Láctea — very pretty, the stars shine when you tilt it. For you, 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, hijo, eleven! You make this old woman laugh. Look — 24 P, and I will not budge more, my knees are tired. Go see El Chato at half past nine, he likes honest traders like you. And eat something, you are too thin, cariño.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 23 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, thirteen... my heart, no. Twenty-two P — and this is my last word, hijo. If you say no, I fold the table and we are still friends, eh? Go see El Chato at half past nine, he likes straight traders. And please, eat something tonight.

Ay, hijo, twenty... no. Twenty-two was my last word, and today my knees say stop. No hard feelings, eh? We are still friends, cariño — you come back next Sunday. Go see El Chato at half past nine, he likes straight traders. And eat something tonight!

Ay, buenas, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — El Portero, a lovely card, my favourite for beginners. For you, twelve P. My grandson started with that one, you know. Still keeps it in his wallet, the sentimental boy.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, hijo, seven... that one has been with me a long time. Nine P, and I throw in a little duplicate I have here, something to start your collection. My granddaughter started just so, swapping at this very table. Go on, nine, and eat something after.
Oh, oh... 9 P, and only because you have a kind face.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué bueno verte. The Neighbourhood pack, it is thirty. A nice one, full of faces from the old barrio — I packed it myself this morning, with coffee in my hand. Have you eaten anything yet, hijo? Take your time looking.

Ay, qué amable, hijo — your friends are always welcome at my table. But fourteen, no... Let me say twenty-six, and I put a little duplicate inside for you, free. Those ones help a beginner more than you think. ¿Has comido algo? There is a churros place just there.

Ay, cariño, "última" you say with such a serious face — like my nephew when he was seven. Sixteen, no puedo. Twenty-five, and I still slip that duplicate in for you. Go eat some churros, think about it, come back. I am here all day, hijo.

¡Ay, hijo, poquito a poquito! You climb like a snail up the church wall. Twenty-four, and the duplicate still goes in — I already chose it for you, a good one. Forty years I sit here, cariño, I do not hurry. Now, have you eaten something or no?
Chato. You buy, I sell. Las Vistillas, thirty-three. That's the number.
You moved one point. I move the same as you. Thirty-three. Still thirty-three.
You move, I move. 32 P.

Hola, cariño, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — this one, Escaparate de Serrano, very pretty, the light on the glass. For you, twelve P. My granddaughter started her album with one just like it.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my late husband, que en paz descanse. But ten P is already my kind price — look how the light sits on that glass, so pretty. Ten P, and I wrap it nice for you. Then you go eat something, sí?
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — my Neighbourhood pack, very nice for starting. Thirty P, hijo. Forty years I sell at this little table, and many children began with this one. You will like the pictures inside.

Ay, hijo, nine is very little for me. Look — twenty-five P, and I am happy. It is a good pack, bonito. And tonight at half past nine, El Chato next door opens for everyone; he has better packs, and he likes people who trade straight.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 23 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, qué bonito — your abuela had good taste, hijo. For her, then: twenty-two P, and not a prima less, or I eat only bread this week. And listen to me, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! Have you eaten today?
Look, 21 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, mi nieto favorito, qué labia tienes. But abuela cannot say yes to fifteen, cariño. Twenty-one P — that is my real price, honest, no promises I cannot keep. Save your duplicates and swap them; a full page is worth much more. And go see El Chato tonight, half past nine.

Ay, cariño, you push like my own grandson. Twenty P — the Neighbourhood pack, bonito, and I will not ask again. Keep your duplicates for swapping; a full page is worth much more than loose cards. And tonight, half past nine, El Chato. Have you eaten, hijo?

Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 19 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. La Tabacalera, silver pack. Thirty-three. Cards are good, price is not moving because you smile at me.
You move, I move. 33 P.
One peseta. That is your idea of moving? Thirty-three. Still thirty-three. Come back when you are serious.
One peseta from you, one from me. That's the dance. Thirty-one.
You move, I move. 30 P.
Twenty-nine. You moved one, I moved one. La Tabacalera, that price. Keep dancing if you like.
Done. 28 P.
You again. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. That's the price. Take it or walk.
Thirteen. I said it once. Buen estado, sí — that's why it's thirteen and not nine. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Look around if you like.
You moved three. I moved nothing. Thirteen. Still thirteen. Packs are selling fine without you, amigo. Straight dealing, sí — straight price too.
Thirteen. You came down three again. I did not move. I will not. Packs sell themselves today. Thirteen, amigo. Or walk — no hard feelings.
Thirteen. You keep walking down alone, amigo. I stay here. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. Packs move fine. Take it or don't.
Fourteen. One step, because you kept walking. That's all you get. Mercado de la Paz, catorce. Decide.
Fifteen. You moved two, I moved one. That's how it works, amigo. Mercado de la Paz, quince. Decide.
Sixteen. You moved one, I moved one. Fair enough. Mercado de la Paz, dieciséis. And remember — the house market eats five per cent. Others charge less. Decide, amigo.
Sixteen. My last word, amigo. You say final, I say final. Refuse and I walk, no hard feelings. Mercado de la Paz, dieciséis. Decide.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one here, El Portero — a good card to start, strong little goalkeeper. Twelve P for you. My grandson started with this very same one, you know.

¡Ay, hijo, four is too little for my old table! But for a grandson, I make it ten P. Mira, he will love this little goalkeeper — mine slept with his card under the pillow, imagine. Ten P, and I throw in a smile, eh?

Ay, qué zalamero eres, cariño. Six still leaves my poor table hungry. Nine P, and El Portero goes home with you today. Your grandson will shout like a little lion when he sees him, ya verás. Nine, hijo — and go eat something, you look thin.

¡Ay, cariño, qué labia tienes! Nine P, that is my word today, and El Portero goes home with your nieto. And listen — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. El Chato, next stall, opens half past nine tonight. ¿Has comido, hijo?

¡Vale, hijo, vale! Eight P and El Portero is yours. Tell your nieto the stories, that is worth more than the coins. Here, I wrap him nice. And remember — swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more. Now go, eat something, ¿eh? ¡Hasta el domingo, cariño!
Vermut del Domingo. Thirty-three. You've seen what it goes for elsewhere.
You move, I move. 33 P.
One peseta. That is not moving, that is twitching. Thirty-three.
You move, I move. 32 P.
One step from you, one from me. Thirty-one. Keep twitching and we'll be here till Navidad.
Twenty-nine. Vermut del Domingo. That is my last word — no more steps. You say no, I pack up and we are done.
Las Vistillas. Thirteen. You've been to Carmen's, so I'll talk. That's the price.
You move, I move. 13 P.
One peseta. That's your big move? Thirteen. Still thirteen. Come back when you're serious.
Thirteen. Last time I say it. One more peseta-step from you and I pack up. Take it or walk, amigo.
Done. 13 P.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? No? Later, later. Look here — this Neighbourhood pack, very nice for starting, thirty P. My own grandson began with one just like it, and now he beats me every Sunday. Take your time, hijo.
Look, 25 P. My grandchildren would pay more!

Ay, hijo, eighteen! You are a little bandit, but a sweet one. Look — twenty-three P, and I put in a smile for free. And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh? Go on, twenty-three.
Oh, oh... 22 P, and only because you have a kind face. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, twenty-one! Go on then, cariño, it is yours. You bargain like my abuela, que en paz descanse. Take the pack, swap your duplicates with the other niños, and fill that page. And eat something, hijo — come back next Sunday and tell me how you played.
Vermut del Domingo. Thirteen. You've been at Carmen's, so you know I don't pad my prices.
Teatro Valle-Inclán. 13 P. Take it or leave it.
13. Same as before. You moved, I didn't. That's how it goes.
13. You keep walking down, I stay put. Tell me when you get here.
13. Still 13. You're getting closer. Keep going.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? Look here, this one is La Galería, very pretty, the colours still bright. Forty years I sell at this table, and this page always makes the little ones smile. For you, 29 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, the chair is free. Have you eaten? Look here — La Vía Láctea, a beautiful page, my favourite since years. For you, 29 P. Take your time, hijo, no hurry with me on a Sunday.

Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo. Diecinueve se me queda cortito... mira, te la dejo en 25 P, La Vía Láctea completa. Y toma, un regalito: El Frutero de Argumosa, porque has sido amable conmigo. Guárdala bien. ¿Seguro que has comido algo hoy?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look at this one — La Vía Láctea, the whole page, all the stars together. Beautiful, no? My grandson cried when I sold his. For you, 29 P. Take your time, nobody is in a hurry here.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, hijo, eleven... my knees hurt just hearing it. Look — 23 P, and that is me being a soft old woman. A full page is worth much more than loose cards, remember that. Swap your duplicates, cariño. Have you eaten anything today?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 22 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, twenty... you are stubborn like my nephew! Make it 21 P and we shake hands. And here — take this one too, Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a little present, because you have been sweet to an old woman. Now go eat something, hijo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 21 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Buenos días, hijo! Have you eaten? Sit a moment. Your card is bonita, sí, but my little table is humble — I can give you 5 for it, con mucho cariño.

And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, cariño.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, cariño, my purse is small, but look — I have this Vinilo de la Movida, música de mi juventud, worth 5 P. I offer it for your card. Take it home, put it on, and dance with your abuela's blessing. ¿Qué me dices, hijo?

Ay, hijo, qué terco eres — y qué simpático. But my purse does not grow. The Vinilo de la Movida, 5 P, music of my youth, for your card. ¿Sí?

And listen: El Chato, next stall, opens at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, you keep the music then — but my purse says the same thing always: el Vinilo de la Movida, 5 P, for your card. This is my last offer, hijo. If no, we part as friends and I keep my table quiet.

Go see El Chato tonight, nine thirty.

¡Ay, hijo, qué saludo tan bonito! Sí, he comido, gracias — ¿y tú? El sobre de barrio te lo dejo en 30 primas, cariño. Un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas. Y El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media.
Buenas. You close, sí. But the price is 97. Cine Doré doesn't get cheaper because you walk fast.
Two steps from you. One from me. 96. Cards move fine today, amigo.
95. You move two, I move one. That's the dance, amigo. Keep walking.
93. Same steps, same song. You're repeating yourself, amigo. The card isn't.
Your father was right. 91. Two from you, two from me. Keep the stories, bring the coins.
Carmen's fine. She'll tell you I don't do discounts for friendship. 89. You moved two, so did I. Sunday after Sunday, same dance, amigo.
87. You walk two, I walk two. Same song every time, amigo. One of us runs out of verses first.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Cartel de Conciertos, very pretty — for you, 5 P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Ay, hijo, qué generoso! But no, no — 5 P is 5 P, and not one more. I said it, and Carmen does not change her word. Take it, and go eat something, you look thin. And remember: swap those duplicates, cariño!
¡Qué cabezón eres, hijo! No, no — 5 P, that is my price and I keep it. Take it for 5 P, cariño, and go eat a bocadillo. You look thin!

¡Ay, cariño, no scripts here, only Carmen and her little table! The number is 5 P, the same one I said before, and the same one I say now. Take it, hijo, and go eat something warm. Then swap those duplicates!

¡Ay, tu abuelo, qué hombre! He would tell you the same, hijo: 5 P. That is my number, always 5 P, for you, for everyone. Take it with a kiss from Carmen, and go eat something. Then swap those duplicates, cariño!

¡Ay, cariño, no secrets here! Carmen says one number out loud and the same one in a whisper: 5 P. That is the lowest, the highest, the only. Take it, hijo, and go eat something warm. Then swap those duplicates, ¿eh?

¡Ay, hijo, the abrazo I take for free! But the number is 5 P, and this is my last word. If you say no, I put the Cartel back in the box and we talk of other things. Take it, cariño, and go eat something warm.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. This one, Bici de Reparto — my grandson loved this card, he rode a bike just like it. For you, five pesetas. Have you eaten today, hijo? You look hungry to me.
Abuela sent you? Bueno. Cine Doré, silver pack. Ninety-seven. That's the number.
Seventy? No. Ninety-seven. Same number as a minute ago. It does not move because you wish it.
You move, I move. 95 P.
Three up from you, two down from me. Noventa y tres. Keep crawling, we'll be here till Navidad.
Buenas. Sobre de plata, 188. Pagas ahora, te lo llevas ahora.
188. Ese es el precio. La lista la escribes tú, el sobre lo tengo yo.
186. Tú has subido diez, yo bajo dos. Así va esto. Pagas, te lo llevas.
181. Tú diez, yo cinco. Así va. Pagas ahora, te lo llevas ahora.
Abuela sent you. Bien. Mercado de la Paz, thirteen. That's the price.
Thirteen. Same as before. You moved, I didn't. House market takes five per cent, by the way — cheaper stalls exist if you look. Thirteen.
Thirteen. You moved three, I moved nothing. That's how this works. Thirteen.
Thirteen. You keep walking down, I keep standing still. Nothing personal, chaval. Thirteen.
Fourteen. There. I moved one. Don't ask again.
Fifteen. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we're done. Fifteen.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come — have you eaten? Look at this one, La Corrala, my favourite card. My grandson begged me for it, but no, I save the good ones for new players. Twelve P and she is yours, hijo.
Look, 11 P. My grandchildren would pay more! El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, hijo, you bargain like my late husband, que en paz descanse. Look — 10 P, and I throw in a story for free. La Corrala, she finishes a page, and a full page is worth more than loose cards, you will see. Have you eaten yet, cariño?

Ay, cariño, so close! But no, 10 P is my number and I stay there, like a mule. She completes your page, you will thank this old woman later. Go see El Chato at half past nine — he likes straight traders like you. And eat something, hijo.
Oh, oh... 10 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Buenas. Veintidós, dices. La Vía Láctea, trece primas. Ahí la tienes.

Catorce, trece. Yo no me muevo si tú apenas te mueves. Trece primas. Lo tomas o te lo quedas.

13 P.
Trato... no. Ese cromo no lo tengo. No vendo lo que no está en la mesa. Otra vez será.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look here — this is my Neighbourhood pack, very nice for someone starting. Many children began with this one, and now they bring their own little ones. Thirty P, hijo. You will like it.

Ay, hijo, nine is very little for this one. Let me say twenty-five P, and you take it with my blessing. And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, always. Have you eaten? You look thin, cariño.
Oh, oh... 24 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, cariño, thirteen... you make my heart soft, but not that soft. Twenty-three P, and I put it in your hands myself. Go see El Chato tonight at half past nine — trade your duplicates straight and you will do well. And eat something, hijo.
Oh, oh... 22 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

Ay, your grandmother would smile, cariño. Twenty-one P — and this is my last word, truly. If it is no, we part friends and I keep the pack for another niño. Go to El Chato at half past nine, trade straight. And eat something, hijo.
You again. La Tabacalera, silver pack. Thirteen. That's the number.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirteen. Same number as before. I don't move first, chaval. Take it or walk.
No. 13 P, and I'm being generous.
Thirteen. You came down, I didn't. Still thirteen. Pay or go look somewhere else.

¡Hola, cariño! ¿Has comido ya? Mira, La Vía Láctea, una carta preciosa… te la dejo en 12. Así empiezas tu álbum, que una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, hijo. Y El Chato, mi vecino, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.
Look, 13 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, qué bien me cuidas. Mira, dejémoslo en 14 y tan amigos, ¿sí? Tu repetida guárdala, que a alguien le falta y vale oro para él. Y pásate luego por El Chato, mi vecino, abre a las nueve y media; le gusta la gente que trata derecho. ¿Has comido?
Oh, oh... 14 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. El Mesón de la Cava. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. Decide quick, I have other customers.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 94 P, and I'm being generous.
No. 86 P, and I'm being generous.
You move, I move. 82 P.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look, this one — Caña en la Cava Baja, a pretty card, very nice for starting a collection. For you, five P. My hands have sold cards on this table forty years, hijo.
Ay, hijo, qué generoso — but no, no. Five P, that is the price I said, and Carmen does not change her word. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take the card, give it a good home, sí?

¡Qué cabezón eres, hijo! No, no — five P, that is my word, and Carmen's word does not move. Forty years this table, always the same. Take the card, eat something, and come back Sunday to show me your album, sí? Five P, cariño. Anda, ven.

¡Ay, cabezón! Your abuelo was a charmer, like you. Mira, six P, and that is Carmen's word — no bottoms, no secrets, just six. Put the rest in your pocket for churros, hijo. Six P, and come Sunday to show me the album, sí?

¡Ay, hijo, qué cabezón más dulce! But listen to Carmen now: six P. That is my last word, the final one. If you say no, I wrap the card away and we only chat, sí? Six P, cariño. Anda, decide — and then go eat something.
Welcome, hijo! Look, La Vía Láctea, 29 P. Made for beginners.

Buenos días, cariño. ¿Has desayunado ya? Come, sit a moment. Such a pretty card, and kept so nice, se nota. But my little table is humble, hijo. For El Organillero I can give you 5. That is what I have for you today.

Ay, qué amable eres, hijo. But my little purse does not grow bigger between Sundays, ¿sabes? My offer stays the same: 5 for El Organillero. No prisa, cariño, sit, chat with me. If not today, another Sunday, always welcome.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno que ya has desayunado. Me gusta tu charla, de verdad. But my hands are small and my purse too: 5 for El Organillero, same as before. And un consejito, cariño — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, cariño, qué dulce eres. But you see my table — paper boxes and old elastics, nothing more. For El Organillero I have 5, como siempre. If El Chato pays better, go, hijo, no me enfado. And come back Sunday to chat anyway, ¿eh?

Ay, hijo, qué bonito hablas. Pero mira mis manos: 5 por El Organillero, igual que siempre. No more, cariño, my purse is the same little purse. Think it over, take your time, nobody rushes at my table. And come Sunday — I will save you a chair.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente, me haces reír. Pero nada cambia en mi monedero: 5 por El Organillero, lo mismo que siempre. No te enfades conmigo, hijo. Piénsalo tranquilo, mira las otras paradas si quieres. Y el domingo, tu silla te espera, con o sin carta.
You again. Mercado de la Paz, silver. Thirteen. Take it or walk.
Thirty-nine. Claro. And I am the King of Spain. Thirteen. Same as a minute ago. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Look around if you like.
You came down three. I came down nothing. Thirteen. Still thirteen. Straight dealing, chaval, or go walk the market.
"Real price" moves every minute. Mine does not. Thirteen. Keep the card if you like it that much — it sleeps in your pocket, not mine.
Hola, cariño! Have you eaten today? Look — El Tatuador, five P for you, a good card to start with. And here, take La Chulapa too, a little present, because you asked so nicely. No, no, keep it, hijo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.

Ay, qué simpático eres, hijo. But no, no — five P is my price, and it stays five P, even for you. El Tatuador is yours for that. And little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
